thread:
alex: Customer (acct: acme-corp) reporting streaming API cuts out after ~25s idle. Client sees connection close and final partial chunk, then 502 on reconnect. Using Cloudflare in front of ALB -> origin is hosted API. request_id=req_0a1b2c3d link: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/789
maria: Can you paste the request logs + request id? any retry pattern or consistent timing?
josh: Seen this before with CF + ALB + nginx. Often proxy buffers small SSE chunks and then does a half-close. Try curl -v -N to repro and capture pcap.
alex: Repro curl I ran:
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-4o" 
```
Response starts fine, heartbeat lines appear, then after ~24-28s the stream shows no more data and client gets EOF. No 5xx returned from origin.
ingress-bot: env_ref: upstream reset: connection error: stream reset by peer (upstream: 10.2.5.8:443)  
(This is an automated log from frontend proxies.)
maria: Looking at traces: origin kept sending heartbeat ":\n\n" but Cloudflare appears to coalesce/aggregate small chunks. ALB idle timeout is 60s by default but we see cut at ~25-30s which suggests intermediate HTTP/2 windowing or proxy buffering behavior.
josh: Two quick mitigations: 1) disable proxy buffering on nginx (X-Accel-Buffering: no or proxy_buffering off), 2) reduce heartbeat interval to <15s so CF/ALB don't coalesce into bigger frames.
alex: Customer can't control Cloudflare config on their managed plan. They asked for a server-side mitigation from us. We tried decreasing heartbeat to 10s and that improved stability in their tests.
maria: Nginx snippet to recommend for self-hosted frontends (if they run nginx in front of origin):
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
proxy_set_header Cache-Control "no-transform";
```
josh: Also for ALB/NLB: ensure idle timeout > expected heartbeat interval. For ALB use > 90s for safety. For Cloudflare: disable Response Buffering / enable 'Origin Server: Always Online' is not relevant — they need to turn off 'Response Buffering' or set 'Origin Cache Control'. Sending small non-empty bytes helps too (e.g., a space or colon comment) because some proxies drop purely empty keepalives.
alex: Repro steps we recorded for eng-runtime ticket:
1) curl -v -N as above and confirm cut at ~25s
2) tcpdump on origin side: `sudo tcpdump -i any -w sse_acme.pcap host 198.51.100.23 and port 443` (customer IP)
3) compare application-level logs: we see server sends `:heartbeat\n\n` at t=0,15,30 but packets show CF coalescing and then ALB FIN at ~25s
Sample tcpdump excerpt (hex simplified):
```
[TCP] 00:00:24 -> FIN from 198.51.100.23
[TCP] 00:00:25 -> RST from client
```
This suggests proxy half-close before application finished sending.
maria: For short-term support guidance to customer:
- Lower heartbeat to 10s (we pushed a patch they accepted)
- If possible, disable Cloudflare response buffering or set 'Origin Cache Control' to respect
- Set ALB idle timeout >= 90s
- Add headers: `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Connection: keep-alive` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` when possible
josh: I'll open a runtime engineering ticket (INF-1245) to investigate automatic detection of fronting proxies and an optional 'proxy-friendly heartbeat' mode that inserts small no-op chunks at ~10s for hosts behind known proxies (Cloudflare, ALB). Tagging @maria for traces attachment.
maria: INF-1245 created. Attached: curl logs, pcap, request_id=req_0a1b2c3d, and snippet of edge logs. Priority: P2. Requesting eng-runtime to evaluate risk of inserting periodic non-empty chunking in hosted API.
alex: Customer applied heartbeat patch and reported initial improvement. We'll monitor for 24h. If they still see disconnects we'll escalate with pcap to CF support. Thanks all :thumbsup:
